title: Leaving a Program, Removal, Bonus Clawback and Commitment Changes — Demand Response Programs
content:
## Terms of participation

**1. Leaving.** The customer may leave a program of the Demand Response Programs at any time, the exit taking effect under the program's rule on when leaving takes effect; leaving is the customer's own decision. A customer who leaves becomes *unenrolled*.

**2. Bonus clawback.** Leaving within the program's bonus clawback months of activation forfeits the enrollment bonus. A bonus is clawed back once per enrollment. A clawback reduces the enrollment's incentive balance by the bonus taken back.

**3. Removal by the company.** The company removes an enrollment when the count of consecutive non-performing events reaches the program's removal count, when opt-outs exceed the limit where the excess consequence is removal, or when the service agreement closes. A removed enrollment shows the status *removed*.

**4. Commitment changes.** Committed kW changes follow the program's rule on when and how the committed kW may be changed, and are made only on an active enrollment, never below the program's minimum committed kW.

## Counting consecutive non-performing events

The count starts at the enrollment's most recent event record and runs back through its event records, most recent first, for as long as each record shows that the customer did not opt out and that the delivered kW was 0.0. The first record that shows an opt-out, or any delivered reduction, ends the count.

| Hypothetical records, most recent first | Count |
|---|---|
| 0.0 kW not opted out; 0.0 kW not opted out; 0.0 kW not opted out | 3 |
| 0.0 kW not opted out; 0.0 kW not opted out; opted out; 0.0 kW not opted out | 2 |
| 0.0 kW not opted out; 1.2 kW delivered; 0.0 kW not opted out | 1 |
| 2.5 kW delivered; 0.0 kW not opted out | 0 |

A Base Interruptible Program enrollment reaches its removal count at 2; a Smart Thermostat Rewards, Home Battery Dispatch or Commercial Capacity Bidding Program enrollment at 3.

## Removal grounds at a glance

| Ground | Applies where |
|---|---|
| Consecutive non-performing events reach the program's removal count | The program has a removal count (not 0) |
| Opt-outs exceed the season's limit | The program's consequence for excess opt-outs is removal |
| The service agreement closes | Every program |

## Illustrations (hypothetical enrollments)

- An AC Cycling Program enrollment activated on 2025-07-01 is left on 2026-01-15 at the customer's request. That is within 12 months of activation, so the $50.00 bonus is forfeited and clawed back once.
- A Smart Thermostat Rewards enrollment activated on 2024-06-03 is left on 2025-09-10, more than 12 months after activation; no clawback arises.
- A Home Battery Dispatch customer with an active enrollment, who has made no change before the coming season, asks before that season to lower the commitment from 5.0 kW to 3.0 kW. The enrollment is active, this is the one change before that season, and 3.0 kW is not below the program's minimum of 3.0 kW, so the change follows the rule.
- A Commercial Capacity Bidding Program enrollment in enrolled status, not yet active, cannot have its committed kW changed.
